slides.title: Katyayani, the warrior who slays Mahishasura
slides.sub: The sixth form of Durga, worshipped on Shashthi

slides.title: Born in a sage's hermitage
slides.body: Born, in one account, in the hermitage of the sage Katyayana, she is the warrior form who slays Mahishasura. In parts of north India, young women pray to her for a good marriage.

slides.title: Lion, sword and lotus
slides.body: She rides a lion and has four arms: one with a sword, one with a lotus, the others raised in blessing. Today is also Shashthi, when Kolkata's pujas wake the Goddess at Bodhon.

slides.text:
चन्द्रहासोज्ज्वलकरा शार्दूलवरवाहना ।
कात्यायनी शुभं दद्याद्देवी दानवघातिनी ॥
slides.translit: Chandrahasojjvalakara shardulavaravahana, katyayani shubham dadyad devi danavaghatini
slides.meaning: May Katyayani, slayer of demons, whose hand gleams with the moon-bright sword and who rides the noble lion, grant what is good.

slides.title: Day 6 at a glance
items: Short mantra: Om Devi Katyayanyai Namah

slides.title: Shashthi: the day the goddess is woken
Kalparambha
slides.body: Kalparambha means beginning of the rite. The priest makes a formal resolve, the sankalpa, to perform the worship over the coming days, often with a kalash set up as the goddess's seat. It is brief.

slides.title: Bodhon: the awakening
slides.body: Autumn is the gods' night, so the goddess must first be woken, as Rama did. The priest invokes her in a bel tree, or a bel branch in a pot, with mantras, conch shells and ulu, while the dhak plays.

slides.title: Amantran: the invitation
slides.body: After the bodhon the goddess is formally invited to accept the worship of the coming days.

slides.title: Adhivas: the consecration
slides.body: The priest touches the image and the bel branch with auspicious items: earth, fragrance, stone, paddy, durba grass, flowers, fruit, curd, ghee, a mirror, vermilion, a conch. The list varies by tradition.

slides.title: What to look for
items: A bel branch in a pot, tied with red thread
Lamps, flowers and a kalash around it
The dhakis playing for the bodhon
In many pujas, the idol's face unveiled
Many mothers fast for their children

caption.en:
Durga Puja 2026 Shashthi in Kolkata: bodhon, amantran and adhivas, explained 🔔

Shashthi is Saturday 17 October. By day the priest makes the sankalpa of Kalparambha. In the evening the goddess is woken at a bel tree, or a bel branch in a pot, with conch shells, ulu and the dhak.

Then she is invited (amantran) and consecrated (adhivas) with earth, paddy, durba grass, a mirror, vermilion and more. In a number of Kolkata pujas her face is unveiled that evening.

The order and timing follow each family's tradition and the panjika the priest uses, so check with your puja committee.

Where do you watch the bodhon every year? Tell us in the comments 👇

slides.title: Bonedi bari pujas: Kolkata's old family pujos
slides.sub: Thakur dalans, ekchala idols, rites kept for generations

slides.title: A puja in the family home
slides.body: A Durga Puja held by an old Kolkata family in its own ancestral home. You step into a courtyard, and on a raised, pillared thakur dalan stands the goddess with her children in one frame.

slides.title: Ekchala, year after year
slides.body: Durga, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Ganesha and Kartik share one frame under one arch. Families keep the same face, colours and daker or sholar saaj every year, and rituals follow each house's own customs.

slides.title: Names to know
items: Chhatu Babu and Latu Babu Bari

slides.title: Late morning to afternoon
slides.body: Saptami to Navami, late morning to afternoon, when rites are under way and crowds are lighter. Metro to Sovabazar or Shyambazar for most north Kolkata houses. Timings and access change, so check locally.

slides.title: You're a guest here
slides.body: Dress modestly and remove shoes where asked. Don't climb onto the thakur dalan or touch the idol. Ask before taking photos and avoid flash. Keep your voice down during puja, aarti and anjali.

slides.line: Some houses keep their own immersion customs on Dashami

slides.title: Save this for a north Kolkata afternoon

caption.en:
Bonedi bari pujas in Kolkata: the old family Durga Pujas held at home 🪔

Instead of a theme pandal, you step into a courtyard, and on the pillared thakur dalan stands Durga with her children in one ekchala frame. Rituals follow each family's own customs, kept for generations.

Sovabazar Rajbari's puja is traditionally dated to 1757. Rani Rashmoni's house at Janbazar, Laha Bari, Mallick Bari and Dawn Bari are among the best known. Go late morning to afternoon, Saptami to Navami, and remember you're a guest in someone's home.

slides.title: Luchi and alur dom for Ashtami morning
slides.sub: No onion, no garlic, about 20 luchi

slides.title: Dough, potatoes, oil
items: 2 tbsp ghee or oil, for the dough
½ tsp salt and ½ tsp sugar, for the dough
About ½ cup (120 ml) water, plus 1 to 2 tbsp
Oil for deep-frying, about 2 to 3 cups
3 tbsp mustard oil or neutral oil

slides.title: The spices
items: 1 tsp cumin seeds and 2 bay leaves
2 dried red chillies and a pinch of hing
1½ tbsp ginger paste, 2 green chillies, slit
1 tsp each ground turmeric, cumin, coriander
½ tsp garam masala powder and 1 tsp ghee

slides.title: A firm, rested dough
slides.body: Mix the maida, salt and sugar and rub in 2 tbsp ghee. Add water a little at a time and knead 5 to 6 minutes into a smooth, firm dough. Cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes.

slides.title: Boil and fry the potatoes
slides.body: Boil the potatoes 12 to 15 minutes, peel and prick. Fry in 3 tbsp oil with a pinch of turmeric for 5 to 6 minutes; lift out. Crackle the cumin, bay leaves, chillies and hing for 30 seconds.

slides.title: Simmer the dom
slides.body: Cook ginger, green chillies and the ground spices with 3 tbsp water for 3 to 4 minutes, till the oil separates. Add tomato if using. Add potatoes, salt, sugar, 1 cup hot water; simmer covered 10 minutes.

slides.title: Roll and fry the luchi
slides.body: Make 20 balls and roll each to about 10 cm and 2 mm, with oil, not dry flour. Fry one at a time at about 180°C, pressing it under the oil till it puffs. Keep it pale. Serve at once.

caption.en:
Luchi and alur dom recipe, the Durga Puja Ashtami breakfast after anjali, with no onion or garlic 🪔

Many families fast on Ashtami morning, offer pushpanjali, then come home to puffed white luchi and a ginger-spiced potato curry. It's festive and rice-free. That suits homes that avoid rice until the puja is done, though customs vary.

Want luchi that puff? Keep the dough firm and rested, roll with oil instead of dry flour, and fry one at a time at about 180°C. Then eat them the moment they come out.

Save this for Ashtami morning 🙏
